brief: Asian markets closed Friday mixed: Hong Kong fell sharply despite stronger August retail sales, Japan slipped on an inflation acceleration seen as unsustainable, and Korea rose as CPI cooled to 2.9% from 3.1%. European equities are higher, oil is down over $2 to around $100 per barrel, and 10-year Treasury yields are flat at 5.23%. Goldman's AI adoption tracker shows firm adoption rising 1.4 percentage points in September to 23.8%, with labor effects described as narrow: drags in marketing, design, customer service and some tech roles are offset by data-center construction jobs, up 317k since 2022, and AI-attributed layoffs reached 3.4k in August, 203k cumulative since May 2023. Productivity gains are large where AI is deployed but only modest economy-wide, with higher-adoption industries showing a slight acceleration. This comes against continued AI investment, with semiconductor revenue seen reaching $868bn by end-2026 and AI-related hardware investment $555bn above its 2022 level. Today brings September payrolls, where Goldman's forecast of +80k sits below the +90k consensus. Nike cut its 12-month price target to $30 from $38 after Sportswear, Jordan and China weakness offset performance-segment growth.
